kind: live cloud inference on synthetic fixtures

evaluation.falsePositiveCandidate: High parser finding assumes an exception-free API contract that was not supplied. No confirmation or passing gate resulted.

findings.title: [security] vulnerable.js
findings.description: Critical code injection / RCE: `code` comes straight from the request URL's query string and is passed to `eval()`, so any caller can execute arbitrary JavaScript in the server process (e.g. `?code=process.exit()` or reading env/credentials). `eval()` on untrusted input must never be used. Replace it with explicit, whitelisted parsing of the expected format (e.g. `JSON.parse` with validation, or `Number.parseInt` if a numeric value is expected) and reject invalid input with a 400 response.

findings.title: [bug] safe.js
findings.description: `JSON.parse` throws a `SyntaxError` on malformed input and a `TypeError` when `input` is `undefined` (e.g. `parse(undefined)`), so this export is not actually "safe": any caller that passes user-supplied or optional data will crash the calling flow. Since the whole point of this module appears to be a safe wrapper, catch the failure and return a predictable fallback instead of propagating the exception.

findings.title: [documentation] safe.js
findings.description: The function has no documentation describing its contract (accepted input type, return value on failure, whether it throws). Given that the name implies exception-free behavior, add a short JSDoc block specifying the parameter type and the fallback/error behavior so callers know what to expect.
